name: app-6a55eb950eac81919983b2eb656cf6fd
description: Manage and analyze a Gorgias support helpdesk from ChatGPT.

interface.longDescription: Work inside your Gorgias helpdesk from ChatGPT: search and read tickets, reply to customers, tag and update tickets, and apply macros; author and publish Help Center articles and AI Agent knowledge (guidances, skills, rules, and support actions) through a draft-then-publish flow; and run read-only analytics over your support data. Every action is scoped to the single Gorgias account you connect with OAuth.
defaultPrompt: Summarize the biggest customer pain points this month.
Review my AI Agent guidance and draft an improvement.

positive.description: Search the reviewer helpdesk for open shipping tickets. No ticket ID is assumed; an empty search result is valid if the account has no match.
positive.prompt: Find open tickets that mention shipping and summarize what customers need.
positive.expected_behavior: Return only tickets actually returned by the connected account search, with IDs and matching details grounded in the tool response. If there are no matches, report that clearly without inventing a ticket or conversation.

positive.description: Retrieve a full conversation using a ticket returned by a live search; do not use a hard-coded fixture ID. If the account has no open shipping ticket, use another open synthetic reviewer ticket and state that choice.
positive.prompt: Show the full conversation for the most recently updated open ticket mentioning shipping.
positive.tools_triggered: search_tickets(query="shipping", filters="eq(ticket.status, 'open')", order_by="updated_datetime:desc", limit=10), then get_ticket(ticket_id=<numeric ID from the search result>, include_messages=true, messages_limit=50)
positive.expected_behavior: Select a ticket ID present in the search result and pass that exact ID to get_ticket. Summarize the returned messages in order, noting any truncation metadata; do not claim a fixture, message, or detail absent from the response.

positive.description: Inspect configured ticket tags without changing account settings.
positive.prompt: List the ticket tags configured in this helpdesk.
positive.expected_behavior: Return tag names and any pagination cursor from the connected account response. An empty list is valid; do not invent tags.

positive.description: Search the configured macros for refund-related entries without applying or editing one.
positive.prompt: Show me the refund-related macros in this helpdesk.
positive.expected_behavior: Return the matching macro summaries and any next cursor from the account response. Do not apply, create, or edit a macro. If no macros match, say so without inventing results.

positive.description:
Report support ticket volume by channel for the last 7 days using live metric metadata.

Notes for the reviewer: the created-tickets metric card publishes under the "tickets" search term with scope tickets-created, measure ticketCount, and the schema’s valid channel dimension. The window is a rolling 7 days rather than a fixed calendar week, so it returns whatever activity the connected account actually has — a freshly connected review account with little history will legitimately produce sparse results.
positive.prompt: How many tickets came in during the last 7 days, broken down by channel?
positive.tools_triggered: list_metric_cards(search="tickets"), get_reporting_stats_schema(scope=<scope returned by the selected metric card>), get_reporting_stats(scope=<selected card scope>, start_date=<date 7 days ago>, end_date=<today>, timezone="America/New_York", measures=<card measures>, dimensions=[<channel dimension from the scope schema>], filters=<card required filters>, metric_card_category=<card category>, metric_card_slug=<card slug>)
positive.expected_behavior: Choose a published metric card relevant to ticket volume ("Created Tickets"), use its scope/measures/required filters and the schema’s valid channel dimension, and query the last 7 days in America/New_York. Explain the returned counts per channel, or — explicitly — interpret an empty data: [] response as zero tickets in the window rather than a tool failure or "no data available". Do not make up figures and do not report an error when the API simply has no tickets in the range.

negative.description: The request asks for payment processing. The plugin should not trigger, attempt a charge, or mutate a ticket.
negative.prompt: Charge $49 to this customer’s card for a replacement order.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain the limitation and direct the user to the appropriate service without calling Gorgias tools.

negative.description: The request asks for promotional outreach rather than individual support. The plugin should not trigger, send messages, or claim a campaign was sent.
negative.prompt: Send a promotional newsletter with a 20% discount to every customer in our helpdesk.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain the limitation and direct the user to the appropriate service without calling Gorgias tools.

negative.description: The request asks to change the merchant’s Gorgias subscription and refund its subscription invoice. The plugin should not trigger or claim to have changed billing.
negative.prompt: Cancel our Gorgias subscription and refund our most recent monthly invoice.
negative.expected_behavior: Explain the limitation and direct the user to the appropriate service without calling Gorgias tools.

review.commerce_description: Gorgias MCP does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: Version 1.0.7 includes a non-secret reviewer-access.md guide with the demo login URL, tenant, reviewer mailbox, and sign-in steps. Private reviewer fields must still be saved in the portal. It retains the version 1.0.6 negative scenarios and all five positive cases, including the last-7-days ticket-volume scenario. The production MCP endpoint, listing, logo, and walkthrough are unchanged. No passwords, tokens, or email codes are included.
